mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Sunday 4:08 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-13 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: L3Harris Technologies
items.about: L3Harris is a US defense and aerospace contractor that also runs communications systems for the FAA.
items.why: Transportation Secretary Duffy said a router installed in southern Arkansas during L3Harris's copper-to-fiber upgrade of FAA telecom lines may be key to Friday's nearly five-hour nationwide ground stop, which disrupted more than 20,000 flights. The FAA says the root cause isn't established, and the FAA and FBI are examining the equipment at an L3Harris lab. The stock closed Friday at $272.35 before the news fully spread, and posts are debating Monday's open.

items.name: NVIDIA
items.about: Nvidia designs the graphics processors and networking gear used to train and run most AI models.
items.why: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and left the board on Nov 12 after reports of affairs, including one with a woman US officials believe is a Chinese spy; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Shares fell more than 4% that day and another 2% Friday to $162.85, HSBC cut the stock to hold and Bernstein halved its target to $200. Q3 earnings on Tuesday, Nov 17 are the next big test.

items.name: Summit Therapeutics
items.about: Summit is a biotech developing ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF antibody for lung cancer.
items.why: Summit disclosed on Sunday that the FDA issued a complete response letter for ivonescimab plus chemo in EGFR-mutant lung cancer, a day after the Nov 14 goal date, because HARMONi showed no statistically significant overall-survival benefit (HR 0.79, p=0.057). The stock had already slid 6.2% Friday to $14.14, and posts expect a steep Monday drop, while bulls point to HARMONi-3 squamous data due by year-end.

items.name: Grayscale Ethereum Mini Trust
items.about: The Grayscale Ethereum Mini Trust is an exchange-traded fund that holds ether.
items.why: Ether kept sliding over the weekend to about $1,816, down roughly 1% on Sunday per posts, after the trust fell 3.3% Friday. The stream is dominated by bearish chart calls about whether ether can hold the $1,775 area, alongside bitcoin weakness near $64,600.

items.name: Home Depot
items.about: Home Depot is the largest US home-improvement retailer.
items.why: Home Depot reports Q3 before the bell on Tuesday, Nov 17, kicking off a big retail earnings week with Target and Walmart. Posts note first-half comparable sales rose about 1.2%, within its flat-to-2% full-year guide, with growth coming from higher ticket sizes rather than more transactions.

items.name: ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil
items.about: UCO is a leveraged ETF that aims for twice the daily move of crude oil futures.
items.why: The IEA said Friday the oil market is returning to a surplus in Q4 as Gulf exports recover faster than demand, which pressured crude and the 2x long fund fell 1.3%. Posts balance that against Middle East shipping risk, with WTI near $90.

items.name: ProShares UltraShort Bloomberg Crude Oil
items.about: SCO is a leveraged ETF that aims for twice the inverse of crude oil futures' daily move.
items.why: The inverse oil fund rose 1.3% Friday as crude eased on the IEA's call for a Q4 supply surplus. Traders are using it to bet on or hedge against oil after a volatile run tied to Iran tensions.

items.name: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals
items.about: Alnylam develops RNA-interference medicines, including Amvuttra for a rare heart disease.
items.why: Alnylam jumped 5.4% Friday to $165.04 after a steep 2026 slide, with no single news event clearly behind it. Posts point to a Form 4 insider purchase filed Nov 12 and bullish options flow, while others focus on management turnover; Bernstein recently cut the stock to market perform.

items.name: Nasdaq Inc
items.about: Nasdaq Inc runs the Nasdaq stock exchange and sells market data and financial software.
items.why: The stock barely moved (-0.2%), but many posts use $NDAQ as shorthand for the Nasdaq index, which fell Friday on Nvidia's selloff yet still had its best week since August. Chatter mixes the Nvidia CEO exit, Super Micro and the FAA ground stop rather than company news.

items.name: Target
items.about: Target is a US discount retailer selling groceries, home goods and apparel.
items.why: Target reports Q3 this week alongside Walmart and Home Depot, a key read on holiday-season consumer demand. Posts note its Q2 comparable sales rose 3.8%, driven almost entirely by more transactions, and that the stock is up about 60% from its late-2025 low.

items.name: Direxion Daily Junior Gold Miners Bull 2X
items.about: JNUG is a leveraged ETF that aims for twice the daily move of junior gold-mining stocks.
items.why: The 2x junior-miner fund fell 1.5% Friday as gold and silver pulled back with crypto. Posts argue US deficits, including the CBO's reported $409 billion October shortfall, and rising debt costs support gold over time.

items.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR
items.about: XLV is an ETF holding the large US health-care companies in the S&P 500.
items.why: Health care rose 0.5% Friday while tech fell, as posts and a TalkMarkets piece describe money rotating from cooling tech names into defensive sectors. Some posts warn the trade has become crowded, with the ETF well above its moving averages.

items.name: Technology Select Sector SPDR
items.about: XLK is an ETF holding the large US technology companies in the S&P 500.
items.why: The tech ETF fell 2% Friday as Nvidia slid after its CEO's resignation, with traders saying Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings will set the tone for tech next week. Posts also cite scrutiny of chip smuggling to China and pending chip-export bills as a risk to sector earnings.

items.name: Modine Manufacturing
items.about: Modine makes cooling and thermal equipment, increasingly for AI data centers.
items.why: Modine surged 27.9% Friday to $135.66, its biggest gain in six years, after Bloomberg reported Samsung Electronics is in talks to buy the company; neither side has confirmed and no terms were disclosed. Activist Jana Partners also disclosed a stake, and Modine holds an analyst and investor day on Nov 18.

items.name: Alpha Tau Medical
items.about: Alpha Tau develops Alpha DaRT, a radiation therapy that implants alpha-emitting seeds into tumors.
items.why: On Sunday Alpha Tau released interim results from its US REGAIN trial in recurrent glioblastoma: all eight treated patients were alive, and all six evaluable patients responded, five of them completely, at 6.9 months median follow-up. The sample is very small and some responses still need confirmation; the company hosts an investor call Monday at 8:30 a.m. ET.

items.name: WhiteFiber
items.about: WhiteFiber builds and runs AI cloud computing and high-performance data-center capacity.
items.why: WhiteFiber fell 8.8% Friday to $9.43 as AI infrastructure and crypto-linked names sold off, after a wider-than-expected Q3 loss and a B. Riley target cut earlier in the week. Bulls in the stream point to its contracted data-center backlog, while bears call the sector overbuilt.

items.name: Helus Pharma
items.about: Helus Pharma develops HLP003, a drug candidate for major depressive disorder.
items.why: Helus presents topline results from its 223-patient Phase 3 APPROACH study of HLP003 as an add-on treatment for major depression on Monday, Nov 16 at 8 a.m. ET. The drug has FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation, and the stream is full of long-time holders waiting on the binary readout.

items.name: SPDR S&P Biotech ETF
items.about: XBI is an equal-weighted ETF of US biotechnology stocks.
items.why: The biotech ETF dipped 0.4% Friday, and weekend chatter centres on binary events: Summit's FDA rejection, Helus and Alpha Tau data on Monday, and an expected Phase 3 readout from SELLAS. Posts say small-cap biotech could see deal interest after last week's selloff.

items.name: ASML Holding
items.about: ASML makes the lithography machines used to manufacture advanced computer chips.
items.why: ASML held nearly flat Friday at $1,495 while US chip stocks fell, but it sits below its 20- and 50-day averages. Posts flag about $5.1 million of bullish December call buying and debate whether the Nvidia leadership shock and China export scrutiny will hit chip-equipment demand.

items.name: Trulieve Cannabis
items.about: Trulieve is a US multi-state cannabis operator, largest in Florida.
items.why: Trulieve slipped 2.2% Friday to $10.90 while the stream debates the pace of the DEA's marijuana rescheduling hearing. Posts say an upcoming Russell index addition could bring buying of 10-15 million shares and note the stock is up about 25% this year while the MSOS cannabis ETF is down; those index claims are unconfirmed.
